Heard finally by consent of learned counsels appearing for the parties.

2] An order under Section 30(2)(a) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, was issued on 17th July, 2017, was issued prohibiting the manufacture, storage and distribution or sale of tobacco products such as ghutka, pan masala, kharra etc.,

The complaint in the present petitions is that, for violation of the provisions of this order, the respondent No.3 - Commissioner of Police and respondent No. 4 - Superintendent of Police or Police Officials are conducting raid in the business premises of the petitioners and seizing the articles prohibited by such order.

The contention is that,
such action is without jurisdiction and authority.

According to the petitioners, the officers competent under the provisions of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, can only conduct such raid and seizure and to prosecute the persons found voilating the provisions of the order.

3] The question is covered by the decision of the Division Bench of this Court in the case of Ganesh 4 wp24.18+821.18.odt Pandurang Jadhao and anr vrs. State of Maharashtra and ors, reported in 2016 Cri.L.J. 2401.

It is not disputed in the reply filed by the respondents that under the provisions of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, an independent procedure for search, seizure, sampling and the consent of the Commissioner prior to lodging prosecution is provided and the same is mandatory.

It is also not disputed in the reply filed by the respondents that the raid is being conducted by the respondent Nos. 3 and 4 or through their sub ordinate officers and the material found in violation of the order is being seized and the prosecution is launched under the provisions of the Indian Penal Code.
4] In view of the decision of the Division of this Court cited supra and after going through the provisions of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, we are of the view that the action complained of in the present petitions taken at the instances of the respondent Nos. 3 and 4 is without jurisdiction and authority.

The respondent Nos. 3 and 4 or the other police officials have no jurisdiction to carry out raid and seize the prohibited material from the business premises of the petitioners or to launch the prosecution under 5 wp24.18+821.18.odt the provisions of Indian Penal Code.
Needless to say that it is open for the authorities under the said Act to carry out such exercise in accordance with law.
The writ petitions are, therefore, allowed.
Rule made absolute in above terms.
No order as to costs.
